children: The rupee opened at 94.93 per dollar on Monday, compared with Friday's close of 94.94, as elevated crude oil prices and the likely absence of last week's supportive inflows weighed on sentiment.

The rupee traded in a range of 94.32-94.97 last week, finding support from inflows linked to the Jio Platforms IPO and position unwinding. With the IPO allotment scheduled for Monday and listing set for Wednesday, traders expect the associated flow support to fade.

The strong foreign institutional investor demand for the IPO likely generated flows into the spot market, supporting the rupee, bankers said. However, a currency trader at a private sector bank said last week's flow support was unlikely to recur, while elevated oil prices remained a drag on sentiment. This tilted the rupee's risk balance to the downside, with Reserve Bank of India intervention remaining a key factor, the trader added.
Dollar demand from oil refiners is not currently a direct factor, as the RBI's special window allows them to meet their foreign exchange requirements outside the usual market.

However, Brent crude trading near $115 a barrel remains a key macroeconomic concern, worsening the external outlook, driving hedging demand and weighing on foreign portfolio flows. Brent rose more than 6% last week to a six-month high, with ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia keeping supply concerns in focus.

Beyond oil prices, the US Federal Reserve's policy decision is a key focus this week. While a pause is widely expected, markets will look for clues on the rate outlook, particularly the possibility of another rate hike in December.

title: Rupee opens marginally higher at 94.93/$ amid volatility, fading IPO inflows
